messages:
maria: Quick status update — I flipped the FP8 kernel flag for the bakeoff jobs on H100 and L40S (llama-2-70b, AWQ quant). Wanted to surface some weirdness on L40S before we auto-enable everywhere.

maria: TL;DR: H100 runs are clean and give ~0.6-0.9% TPU-normalized perf improvement vs fp16. L40S shows sporadic numerical instability at long seqs (>2048): rare NaNs + 0.3-0.7% increase in ppl on standard evals. Not consistent across seeds.

jon: Can you paste the failing run id / minimal repro?

maria: repro command (use the bakeoff harness):
```
./run_bakeoff --model llama-2-70b --quant awq --precision fp8 --device l40s --seq_len 4096 --batch 1 --seed 42 --run-id r2026-l40s-fp8-01
```
Observed stack snippet:
```
RuntimeError: kernel_accumulate(): NaN detected in row 1932
  at /workspace/runtime/kernels/fp8_matmul.cu:214
```

sahil: Hmm, that stack points at the accumulation path. H100 uses fused-accumulate that does internal fp32 accumulator with different rounding. L40S kernel uses a narrower accumulator in the current build? Could be a casting/order-of-ops difference.

kp: We have a couple of differences in kernel flags between builds: H100 got `--enable-fp8-accum-wide` and L40S didn't because of a previous perf regression. IIRC the L40S fallback uses pairwise accumulation with lower dynamic range.

maria: Numbers from runs (median of 5 seeds):
- reference (fp16): ppl=6.84, exact-match=86.7%
- AWQ+INT8: ppl=6.92 (+1.2%), em=86.1% (-0.6%)
- FP8 on H100: ppl=6.79 (-0.7%), em=86.9% (+0.2%)
- FP8 on L40S: ppl median=6.86 (+0.3%), but 2/5 seeds showed NaN crashes or ppl jumps to 7.03 (+2.8%)

maria: So FP8 can be better on H100 but flaky on L40S for long-context workloads.

jon: Could this be an activation scaling issue? Did the AWQ quant use per-tensor vs per-channel scaling?

sahil: AWQ uses per-channel for weights, but activation scaling is runtime-managed. We recently increased the amax window from 64->256 to reduce quantization churn; that could make amax lag on long tails, causing overflows. Try shrinking the tracking window and enabling stochastic rounding for L40S.

maria: I re-ran with amax_window=64 & stochastic_round=true. Repro command:
```
./run_bakeoff --model llama-2-70b --quant awq --precision fp8 --device l40s --seq_len 4096 --amax_window 64 --stochastic_round yes --run-id r2026-l40s-fp8-02
```
Result: stability improved, no NaNs in 5 seeds, ppl now 6.82 (+0.3%) stable. Still not as good as H100 but acceptable.

kp: That supports the hypothesis. L40S kernel accum path + larger amax window = occasional clipping. We should treat activation scaling as a runtime knob per-device.

jon: For rollout policy — recommend we do NOT flip auto-enable for L40S yet. Instead:
1) Add device-specific runtime profile that forces amax_window=64 and stochastic_round by default for L40S FP8.
2) Add CI gating: a long-context stability test (seq_len=4096, 10 seeds) for FP8 on L40S.
3) Instrument to capture amax traces and a small histogram for 1% of requests so we can detect drift in prod.

maria: I'll open the PR with the profile and add the CI job. Want to add an opt-in flag in console first (so enterprise customers can try it).

sahil: Also consider mixed-precision fallback for the softmax/attention kernels: keep matmuls in FP8 but run softmax/gelu in FP16 for L40S when seq_len>2048. That avoids accumulation edge-cases while keeping most perf wins.

kp: Good call. We already have a pathway to mark per-op precision in the runtime config. Adding a conditional rule `if device==L40S and seq_len>2048 -> attention_softmax_fp16` should be straightforward.

maria: Action items I will do: open PR for L40S profile + CI (r2026/profiles#12), add console opt-in, add a recipe for per-op fallback. ETA EOD tomorrow.

jon: I'll pair on the CI job and add a quick dashboard for amax histograms.

ml-ci-bot: CI run queued: r2026/profiles#12 -> test_fortitude_l40s_fp8 (seq=4096, seeds=10). ETA ~35m.

sahil: Meanwhile we should document the known mixed-precision pitfalls: accumulation width differences across GPUs, amax tracking window effects, and per-op rounding/ordering. Add to the bakeoff README.

maria: Yup — I'll add a short section in the repo under docs/bakeoff/fp8-troubleshooting.md with reproduction steps and suggested knobs.

jon: For visibility — tagging @eng-runtime and @product to avoid surprise when we enable per-device defaults.

kp: If CI is green we can ship the runtime profile as opt-in. Full auto-enable only after one week of canary telemetry.

maria: Thanks team. Will post the PR link here once ready. :thumbsup:

ml-ci-bot: CI update: test_fortitude_l40s_fp8 started (run-98321).
